text: [Charming Smile] Not me. I'd make a poor show.

speaker: Coyle's Regulars
text: [Back away.]

text: One of them keeps wrapping his hands and does not look up. "Coyle pays for a good show. You in, or just looking?"

speaker: Ceria
text: Back to the camp rules.

speaker: Ceria
text: Fair enough.

speaker: Ceria
text: Pisces. He's ours. He bills the team by invoice, and the roster carries four names with the hours split four ways. He takes his in the city with a treatise open, which is exactly where I want him until there's something down here worth reading. Three of us hold the shovels. That was the trade, and he argued it well.

speaker: Ceria
text: Let's open it up.

speaker: Ceria
text: Who else is on this crew?

speaker: Ceria
text: You made it. Camp rules: nobody touches anything shiny, nobody wanders past the survey stakes alone. The sealed level's below the pedestal court. We found the site off an old expedition ledger — half the pages are about what they didn't bring out. It's in my tent, filed with the survey maps.

speaker: Ceria
text: See you there.

speaker: Ceria
text: East past the gate road, across the floodplains — follow the survey stakes. Ask for me at the camp. And bring your own rope.

speaker: Ceria
text: What's down there?

speaker: Ceria
text: Word travels. Yes — there's a ruin out past the floodplains, and under it a level nobody's opened since before Liscor had walls. We hit the seal three days ago. Yvlon can't cut it, and the one mage in this city who could read it works for himself and charges accordingly. We need one more pair of hands.

speaker: Ceria
text: If I knew, I wouldn't need a dig. Whatever it is, someone sealed it on purpose and did a very good job. Usually that means valuable or it means dangerous. I plan the camp for dangerous.

speaker: Ceria
text: Go on.

speaker: Ceria
text: Heard your team's digging east of the gate road.

speaker: Ceria
text: Understood.

speaker: Ceria
text: You're the one Olesm's paying to poke the gallery? Good. The Guild sent us along to make sure you come back out. Ceria Springwalker — Horns of Hammerad.

speaker: Ceria
text: All right. Four of us on the roster, three of us actually walking in — Pisces bills from a distance. Try to keep up.

speaker: Ceria
text: It was guarding a door. Wonderful. Somebody left a construct in the dark to watch one door, and we still don't know what's on the other side.

speaker: Ceria
text: Still can't believe we carried that thing across the floodplains. Erin's already put a tablecloth on the pedestal guardian.

speaker: Ceria
text: Let's go.

speaker: Ceria
text: Give me a moment.

speaker: Ceria
text: Rules are simple. Traps kill more adventurers than monsters do, so nobody touches anything shiny. See something worth grabbing, you call me over and you wait.

speaker: narrator
text: I'm in. Where's the camp?

speaker: Stray Corusdeer
text: [Strike first.]

speaker: Stray Corusdeer
text: [Basic Command] Steady it. Slow words, open hands.

speaker: Stray Corusdeer
text: Steady it. The herd knows your hands now.

speaker: Stray Corusdeer
text: [Back away.]

speaker: Stray Corusdeer
text: A shape lifts its head from the tall grass, antlers catching the light — oaken-brown fading to a glow at the tips, cherry-red and warm enough to see the air shimmer above them. It watches you. One ear turns back toward the herd, then returns to you, and stays.

speaker: Boulder Shapes
text: [Strike first.]

speaker: Boulder Shapes
text: [Back away.]

speaker: Boulder Shapes
text: One of the boulder shapes grinds upright — plates of grey stone sliding over something alive underneath. Sand pours out of the joints. It starts toward you at a walk and does not speed up.

speaker: Pisces
text: How far can it actually go?

speaker: Pisces
text: One thing at a time.

speaker: Pisces
text: Mounted and hinged. Observe — already holding a hop to Liscor's gate district, and nobody has offered it so much as a rune of encouragement. It works. The next test is range.

speaker: Pisces
text: Then let's start.

speaker: Pisces
text: Farther than Liscor. The wardwork is straining for distance; set a palm to the frame and you can feel the pull. But push it unattuned and things we did not invite will leak through. So we attune it properly. Krshia stocks the catalysts, and I have already started on the calculations for our half of the work.

speaker: A Frazzled Drayman
text: Good luck with the cart.

speaker: A Frazzled Drayman
text: Slow. Right. Pin came loose past the gate, cart's been dragging since, which means it's under the load. Never hit the road. Huh. I'll get the boards down and dig it out. Sergeant's been shouting at me for an hour and got less done.

speaker: A Frazzled Drayman
text: Breathe. Start at the axle-pin — walk me through it once, slow.

speaker: A Frazzled Drayman
text: Your cart, your problem.

speaker: A Frazzled Drayman
text: Half a day! Half a day stuck behind the market row and now the axle-pin's walked off somewhere and the Watch says move along. Move along where, exactly? Nobody. Nobody is listening.

speaker: A Frazzled Drayman
text: Found the pin. Right where you said to look — wedged under the load, hard up against the axle. I owe you a quiet word for that. Cart's off the row and rolling before dusk.

speaker: Sergeant Ashgrave
text: Put in again.

speaker: Sergeant Ashgrave
text: That's all for now.

speaker: Sergeant Ashgrave
text: Logged and counted. Lamp oil first — the Watch's night patrol has been burning dregs for a week. Then bandages, then a spare gambeson for the next green recruit. The gambeson may have to wait for the next levy.

speaker: Sergeant Ashgrave
text: I'll take a look.

speaker: Sergeant Ashgrave
text: Pell. Green, keen, checks every noise personally instead of logging it and moving on. Went to look at scratching in the drainage gallery two musters back. Hasn't reported since. Not panicking yet. Ask me again after next muster.

speaker: Sergeant Ashgrave
text: Just checking in.

speaker: Sergeant Ashgrave
text: Heard a recruit's gone missing.

speaker: Sergeant Ashgrave
text: I found Pell. Safe, just turned around.

speaker: Sergeant Ashgrave
text: Something toward the Watch's supply fund. (10 gold)

speaker: Sergeant Ashgrave
text: If you're here to report something, report it plain. You do the talking, the belt-slate writes it down.

speaker: Sergeant Ashgrave
text: The supply fund's the better for your coin. Boots this month, bandages when the next crate comes in. The Watch counts you a friend.

speaker: Sergeant Ashgrave
text: Heard what you've been studying. Keep it out of my barracks and off my streets, and you and I stay civil.

speaker: Sergeant Ashgrave
text: Still no word from Pell. Kit's counted twice over on account of it. Slate stays open till someone finds them.

speaker: Sergeant Ashgrave
text: Pell's back on the roster, thanks to you. Kit's counted, slate's closed. Muster sheet reads full again.

speaker: Sergeant Ashgrave
text: Glad it worked out.

speaker: Sergeant Ashgrave
text: Turned around, unhurt. Slate closes tonight. Four gold, out of my own kit budget — the Guild doesn't pay for finding my own people. Pell owes you a drink they can't afford yet.

speaker: Training Dummies
text: (Leave them be.)

speaker: Training Dummies
text: Two battered Watch training dummies on little wheels. One has a face painted on, mostly worn off at the jaw. Relc runs the drills. Talk to him.

speaker: Erin
text: Maybe I'll ask her.

speaker: Erin
text: Odd? Besides Ceria's whole team leaving at dawn with shovels? She's been going on about some ruin east of here. If you're bored, she was muttering about being short-handed.

speaker: Erin
text: All part of the service.

speaker: Erin
text: Whoa. That was - the table's actually reflective now. I scrubbed at that thing all spring and it never looked like this.

speaker: Erin
text: On it.

speaker: Erin
text: Really? It's the horror show by the west wall. I owe you one - or the table does. [Basic Cleaning]'s already on your bar — number key, then go introduce yourself to it.

speaker: Erin
text: I'll look into it.

speaker: Erin
text: I don't know! That's the fun part. Okay, so — Pisces knows creepy old magic, he's usually by the Guild steps on Market Street being smug at pigeons. Or the frame itself, the grain does a thing — look at it properly if you know how. Or the scratching in my cellar, you could — okay, forget the cellar one. Don't do the cellar one. If you go anyway, bring a weapon and don't tell me about it after.

speaker: Erin
text: Happy to help.

speaker: Erin
text: Selys sent the whole reward back with you? That Drake pretends she's all scales. Free breakfast for a week, I mean it.

speaker: Erin
text: No promises.

speaker: Erin
text: Good! You earned it - goblins and Drake bureaucracy in one afternoon. Just don't spend it all on Krshia's stall.

speaker: Erin
text: Set up a board sometime?

speaker: Erin
text: Back up a moment.

speaker: Erin
text: I'll consider myself warned.

speaker: Erin
text: Heard from who? Okay, yes. I play a little. And by a little I mean I will destroy you and feel great about it. It's the one thing I never have to think about. Board's behind the bar — the black queen's a salt cellar until somebody finds the real one.

speaker: Erin
text: Back up a moment.

speaker: Erin
text: It's a date. The chess kind.

speaker: Erin
text: Deal. Fair warning — Olesm's been practicing for months and I still win. Bring snacks, we'll make an evening of it.

speaker: Erin
text: I'll take a look.

speaker: Erin
text: It went somewhere cold this morning. Cold enough the frame's still wet where I touched it. Nobody was near it when it happened. Can you look? Just stay on this side of it while you do.

speaker: Erin
text: It suits you.

speaker: Erin
text: Back up a moment.

speaker: Erin
text: Fair enough.

speaker: Erin
text: Far. Really far. Like, you can't get there by walking, and believe me, I checked, back at the start. I stopped checking. Anyway! The inn's home now. It has a door and everything, and about half the chairs match. I pick up more whenever a trader has them.

speaker: Erin
text: Back up a moment.

speaker: Erin
text: Staying put.

speaker: Erin
text: Yeah? I keep deciding that on purpose, so it's nice when it lands by accident. Hang on — bread's about done and I have to pull it. Stay put, I'll cut you the end bit.

speaker: Erin
text: Back up a moment.

speaker: Erin
text: Thanks, Erin.

speaker: Erin
text: Sit. Eat. That's an order. New recipe — still testing it, but it should stick to your ribs. Call it +2 HP, every fight until you next sleep. Don't ask me to explain the math.

speaker: Erin
text: You feed it.

speaker: Erin
text: I'll stop putting a hook in it, then.

speaker: Erin
text: The deep end? Nobody catches anything out of that. Krshia says it's been that way since before there was a wall on Liscor. I take a bowl out sometimes and leave it on the flat rock. It's gone by morning. I haven't gone down to watch.

speaker: Erin
text: You've never even seen it.

speaker: Erin
text: Well, yeah, I feed everyone who turns up. If something's been out there long enough to be older than the wall, it has definitely not had a hot meal in a while, and that seems like the sort of thing somebody ought to fix.

speaker: Erin
text: Back to it.

speaker: Erin
text: Right, the Guild.

speaker: Erin
text: Selys is still waiting on that package — the Adventurer's Guild, same as it ever was.

speaker: Erin
text: The package made it. It's the reward you still need to sort out, back at the Guild counter.

speaker: Erin
text: I'll take the package.

speaker: Erin
text: Remind me where Selys needs me?

speaker: Erin
text: So what do I actually do about your door?

speaker: Erin
text: Is the new door behaving itself?

speaker: Erin
text: Something in the pond wouldn't take my line.

speaker: Erin
text: Let me deal with that table. ([Basic Cleaning])

speaker: Erin
text: The table situation is handled.

speaker: Erin
text: You sent it back!

speaker: Erin
text: Delivery's done. I kept the tip.

speaker: Erin
text: I heard you play chess.

speaker: Erin
text: You never talk about where you're from.

speaker: Erin
text: (Take the seat. The cook is already ladling.)

speaker: Erin
text: Anything odd around the inn lately?

speaker: Erin
text: Oh good, someone with working legs! I've got a package for Selys at the Guild - mind running it over? Also the common room is a disaster, don't look at it.

speaker: Erin
text: Kitchen's slowing down for the night, but the door's not locked on you. Sit, stay warm, and think hard before you try the walk back in that wind.

speaker: Erin
text: Selys is still waiting on that package, you know.

speaker: Erin
text: Back already? The inn feels almost manageable since you sorted that delivery. I even got to sit down this morning, for about a minute.

speaker: Erin
text: I know what the road is like. Whatever you fought out there, I'm sure it needed fighting. Just look twice at the next one before you decide what it is. The sign out front isn't coming down.

speaker: Erin
text: Heard you talked the goblins into leaving. Talked. With words. I don't know how you managed it and I don't want the details, I just want it to keep working.

speaker: Erin
text: The order came in full, no thanks to whatever almost happened to it. Lyonette hasn't stopped humming since. Same four notes over and over, and I can't place the song.

speaker: Erin
text: On my way.

speaker: Erin
text: You're a lifesaver! Selys is out the door, past the goblin situation. She's the Drake who looks like she's already done with your nonsense.

speaker: narrator
text: Wait, one more thing!

speaker: Miscalibrated Golem
text: [Strike first.]

speaker: Miscalibrated Golem
text: [Detect Magic] Read the rune-fault. Still it at the source.

speaker: Miscalibrated Golem
text: [Back away.]

speaker: Miscalibrated Golem
text: A stone shape at the edge of the forge-heat turns too fast, cracks glowing brighter along its arms — one of the tier's own constructs, off its command spells again. Its head-block swings to you, to the crates, back to you. The second swing is faster.

speaker: Calibration Rig
text: [Bring it back into tolerance the hard way.]

speaker: Calibration Rig
text: [Stand out of its correction and leave it.]

speaker: Calibration Rig
text: The rig registers you, corrects a half-beat late, and registers you again. Its gauges swing past their own marks and settle wrong. Three of the four needles disagree. The fourth is not moving at all.

speaker: Small Shapes in the Dark
text: [Strike first.]

speaker: Small Shapes in the Dark
text: [Back away.]

speaker: Small Shapes in the Dark
text: The seal on the far arch is cracked, and whatever leaked from it has run down the stone and pooled at the base. What little light gets past the rubble sits on the wet patch and on eyes low to the ground, more than a few of them. They are feeding at the leak.

speaker: Goblin Warband
text: Move on.

speaker: Goblin Warband
text: A long pause. The lead goblin sniffs, then spits sideways. A wave, and the others clear the road. They keep their eyes on you until the corner.

speaker: Goblin Warband
text: Draw steel.

speaker: Goblin Warband
text: Stand aside. I've killed things bigger than your whole warband. (Warrior)

speaker: Goblin Warband
text: (Back away slowly.)

speaker: Goblin Warband
text: The goblins fan out across the road, blades low. One eyes your gear, weighing something.

speaker: Grimalkin
text: "Two hours is light?"

speaker: Grimalkin
text: "I'll leave you to your rest day."

speaker: Grimalkin
text: Sit down properly if you are going to sit. Hips back, chest up, and stop hovering. I am off duty. Off duty means today's session was light. Two hours. Sled drags and stair work, logged.

speaker: Grimalkin
text: "Tell her gently, Magus."

speaker: Grimalkin
text: Two hours at half my working load. The volume came down by half as well. The intent does not change. And I am still working, since you ask. Fourteen people have stood up out of a chair since I sat down. Five did it correctly. The tall one clearing tables has better hip mobility than half my Pallass intake and has no idea. I intend to tell her before I leave. She will not thank me.

speaker: Grimalkin
text: "Yes, Magus."

speaker: Grimalkin
text: Good. All of it, while it is hot. Then water, a full cup. Rest before you load again — skip the recovery and the second set is worse than the first. Sit. Heels under you, back straight. Eat something yourself.

speaker: narrator
text: Set a full bowl down in front of him. (Serve)

speaker: Hedault
text: "Understood."

speaker: Hedault
text: Stand where I put you and keep your hands flat on the cloth. Now read it back to me. If you are wrong, I will stop you. There. The ward wants to sit under the setting. It has ignored the stone from the first weighing. Keep your hands flat while I mark the line.

speaker: Hedault
text: Go on, then.

speaker: Hedault
text: Another time. Keep the reading.

speaker: Hedault
text: Hold still. There is a residue on your sleeve I do not see twice in a decade. Ruin warding. A set ward would have gone quiet years ago; this one is fed, and the draw is live. Looking costs nothing.

speaker: Hedault
text: Hold still. There is a residue on your sleeve I have catalogued exactly once before — in this shop, on the fragment you handed me. Ruin warding. A set ward would have gone quiet years ago; this one is fed, and the draw is live. Looking costs nothing.

speaker: Hedault
text: Understood.

speaker: Hedault
text: A set ward holds a shape. A fed ward has to be sourced, continuously, from somewhere with capacity. Whoever hung that frame did not hang it alone, and I have measured what it pulls. Nothing in your pantry pulls that. I will not speculate further in a shop. Bring me the setting when you know, and I will price the work correctly.

speaker: Hedault
text: "That's enough."

speaker: Hedault
text: Forty years ago somebody took the stone and left the glass, and did it well enough that the family never thought to ask. Do not expect the thief to still hold it. Stones of that quality get sold on. There is a man with a back door off the alleys and a ledger he would not show the Watch. I do not go there. You have the address. I have a mount to cut.

speaker: Hedault
text: Fair trade.

speaker: Hedault
text: Hold. Turn it — there. Ruin warding, and well past apprentice work. The same discipline set the frame you woke on your pantry door; one school, long dissolved, and I will not guess at names in a shop. The setting is yours. The fragment stays with someone who can read it properly.

speaker: Hedault
text: "She's known since she was nineteen. She wants the setting held, and the stone left as it is."

speaker: Hedault
text: [Appraise Goods] Read it out with him, weight by weight.

speaker: Hedault
text: [Detect Magic] Follow the ward-line to where it wants to sit.

speaker: Hedault
text: "Somebody swapped it. Who buys a stone like that?"

speaker: Hedault
text: "I'll come back with an answer."

speaker: Hedault
text: Set it on the cloth. Do not hand it to me. I have looked at it twice already and I will not cut a mount until somebody in this transaction says the true thing out loud: that stone is glass, cut well, sold badly, and about forty years old. I will not cut a mount over a lie. It is half-drawn on the bench behind me, and it stays half-drawn until I hear it.

speaker: Hedault
text: "She'll be glad of the price."

speaker: Hedault
text: Good. Then it goes on the order in those words and the price changes, downward, because glass takes less holding than a stone does. A mount for glass is not a lesser commission. It is a different one, and I would rather be told than discover it at the bench.

speaker: Hedault
text: The traveler's charm. Improve it. (20 gold)

speaker: Hedault
text: The hunter's fang. Make it more than a trophy. (35 gold)

speaker: Hedault
text: The wardstone bead. Set it true. (40 gold)

speaker: Hedault
text: The guardian's fragment. I'm told you'd want to see it.

speaker: Hedault
text: Just looking.

speaker: Hedault
text: You've stopped mid-appraisal. What are you looking at?

speaker: Hedault
text: A lady's heirloom. She was told you'd refuse it.

speaker: Hedault
text: State the item and keep your hands where I can see them. First I appraise. Then I correct, if correction is warranted, and I charge exactly what the work is worth.

speaker: Hedault
text: Understood.

speaker: Hedault
text: Done. The work is correct; it is on the cloth and the fee is as quoted. Do not thank me or shake my hand. And keep it away from street enchanters afterward.

speaker: Cups
text: I'll be back for it.

speaker: Cups
text: Ten. Well. The water's warmer already. Set it on the tray where I can count it. Done, I'll sign. But one cup won't drown a man like Coyle — you want Hellam's grudge on paper next to mine. Come back and say 'pour for three' and I'll have him here, wedding manners and all.

speaker: Cups
text: I'll be back for it.

speaker: Cups
text: Every hat, hm. You know what nobody's ever offered the tea-girl before? Standing. Done. Pour it in ink, I'll sign. But one cup won't drown a man like Coyle — you want Hellam's grudge on paper next to mine. Come back and say 'pour for three' and I'll have him here, wedding manners and all.

speaker: Cups
text: You earned the byline, Cups.

speaker: Cups
text: Done and done. Hellam didn't even finish his cup. Signed and sanded before it cooled. Sealed it himself, then asked could he sign twice. Take the papers wherever names like Coyle's go to be spent. And friend — my own name's in the middle of this one. First time for that. The pot's gone cold.

speaker: Cups
text: Stand with the Brothers, and every hat tips your way. [Charming Smile]

speaker: Cups
text: Ten gold says the water's fine. (10 gold)

speaker: Cups
text: Fair. Forget I asked.

speaker: Cups
text: Not for cups of tea, friend. You want my face on this, you've got to be worth the risk first — and 'worth it' isn't free, is it, given what a hat can turn into round here.

speaker: Cups
text: Swearing's different water, friend. Nobody ever knows who poured a rumor first. A testimony sheet has my name at the bottom, and Coyle pays men to read names. I'd like mine kept where it is.

speaker: Cups
text: I'll see it done.

speaker: Cups
text: Here's the third thing, then, since you keep buying the first two. I owe the Brothers a debt I've been quietly not paying. A chit, is all. But it's got Wilovan's own mark on it, and I'd rather it went back quiet, with you, before anyone's sent to collect it. Carry it to the parlor, quiet as you came by it, and we'll talk about faces.

speaker: Cups
text: The alley boys. What's their round? (1 gold)

speaker: Cups
text: Coyle's counting-house. (1 gold)

speaker: Cups
text: Who in this city hates Coyle enough to say so? (1 gold)

speaker: Cups
text: The men in the hats. (1 gold)

speaker: Cups
text: Anything strange brewing? (1 gold)

speaker: Cups
text: Two cups deep. What's the real price, Cups?

speaker: Cups
text: I need more than rumor. Coyle hired that theft — will you swear to it?

speaker: Cups
text: Pour for three. Set it up with Hellam.

speaker: Cups
text: Just the tea today.

speaker: Cups
text: Tea comes free with the rumor. Rumor's a gold the cup. Sit on the crate — mind the wobble, it's structural. Now. What are we drinking?

speaker: Cups
text: Testimony's steeping — my name on paper by week's end. One cup left in the pot worth pouring, and that's Hellam. Say when.

speaker: Cups
text: Hellam signed, I signed, and for once I'm in the best rumor on the street instead of selling it. Tea's still a gold. Sit, the pot's fresh.

speaker: Cups
text: Good tea, Cups.

speaker: Cups
text: Free tea, then. You'd be surprised how few take just the tea. Sit, drink it while it's hot. Crate's still wobbly — sit to the left and it won't tip.

speaker: Cups
text: Another cup.

speaker: Cups
text: I'll remember the yard door.

speaker: Cups
text: Lamps burn past midnight there two nights before every 'audit' — a man cooking books likes them fresh. Better cup, though. The clerk with the inky cuffs takes his supper out, and props the yard-side door for his return. Props it with a cheese wedge. I have seen the cheese, friend. Costs the same, mind.

speaker: Cups
text: Another cup.

speaker: Cups
text: That's all for today.

speaker: Cups
text: There's talk of a door — an inn door, in some Drake town two hundred miles south — that opens here, when it's minded to. Adventurers swear by it. Me, I say any door that shortchanges two hundred miles of road out of its gossip is a menace to my trade personally. Marvelous, though, if it's true.

speaker: Cups
text: Another cup.

speaker: Cups
text: Good to know. Thanks.

speaker: Cups
text: Wister's Alley boys walk it in pairs, and pairs keep habits. Every round they turn at the fish-drying racks — both heads, every time, like the fish might've moved. That's a whole alley of nobody-looking twice a bell. A patient someone could stroll it like a garden. Drink up.

speaker: Cups
text: Another cup.

speaker: Cups
text: Fair warning. Thanks.

speaker: Cups
text: The Brothers? Sweetest muggers you'll ever meet. Tip the hat, beg your pardon. Then they relieve you of exactly what's owed, to the clip — I've had ruder service in shops. But the whole street knows the arithmetic. Hat on, you talk. Hat comes off, you run.

speaker: Cups
text: Another cup.

speaker: Cups
text: Then I'll go see Hellam.

speaker: Cups
text: Master Hellam — silk trade, salt tongue. Coyle soured their partnership over a warehouse lease, then bought that same lease through a cousin. Hellam keeps the grudge fed and walked like a prize hound. He's wanted to testify against Coyle for years.

speaker: narrator
text: Pour for three, then. Set it up.

speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
text: "Your blotter keeps everything backwards. Including a set of initials that isn't yours to press."

speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
text: That is my— you are looking at my blotter. People do not look at my blotter.

speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
text: "You never said a word."

speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
text: It is a blotter. It blots. If a man reads it and walks west past the tea and finds a table there, I never said a word to him. Remember it that way.

speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
text: "Who has been hiring the blank seal?"

speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
text: [Charming Smile] Ask about the handwriting instead of the name.

speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
text: "I'll buy the hour you were not working."

speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
text: [Appraise Foe] The blotter under his elbow.

speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
text: "Nothing today."

speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
text: The blank seal is eight gold the hour. It goes back in the tray when the hour is up. That is the arrangement, {addr}. Ink and paper are extra.

speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
text: You have what you came for, and the tray is full again. Paper is over there. Ink is behind me.

speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
text: "That's an answer."

speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
text: Eight gold, and the hour is yours. What I have is small. I never saw who I wrote for. The seal came back to the tray with alley grit still in the cut, and there is exactly one man west of the tea who works out of an alley and can afford this shop.

speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
text: "That will do."

speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
text: Then there is no confidence to keep. A confidence is a thing a client tells me, and this man was a renter who never said what he was renting. He works a table at the west end of the alleys, past the tea. He pays in coin and he pays late. That's all I know about him.

speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
text: "It's about somebody wearing a house's initials by the hour."

speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
text: Handwriting. Well. Handwriting I can talk about, I suppose. Go on and be charming. It is usually about paper.

speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
text: "Fair enough."

speaker: A Scribe by the Hour
text: No. Coin doesn't change it. Neither does the manners, and I'll thank you for them anyway. The seal goes out and the hour goes in the book. Nothing else gets written down. No names. The day people stop believing that, I have not worked out what I do next.

speaker: A Woman Who Came in a Carriage
text: Thirty gold, counted out flat on the table with no purse and no flourish, by a woman who has plainly never once had to check the count.

speaker: A Woman Who Came in a Carriage
text: "Then we're square."

speaker: A Woman Who Came in a Carriage
text: "Give me a moment with it."

speaker: A Woman Who Came in a Carriage
text: Good. Then he was selling it, and nobody had to take it from him, and the lady kept enough of the name to be worth the theft. That will go back exactly as you said it and not one word further. She is paid for her trouble and you are paid for yours. My mistress does not do favours. She does accounts, and she settles them the same week.

speaker: A Woman Who Came in a Carriage
text: "You bought the block off him."

speaker: A Woman Who Came in a Carriage
text: "He handed it over himself. He wanted it called destroyed. It isn't."

speaker: A Woman Who Came in a Carriage
text: "He never noticed it leave the table."

speaker: A Woman Who Came in a Carriage
text: "I went through his two men and took the block."

speaker: A Woman Who Came in a Carriage
text: "Who sent you?"

speaker: A Woman Who Came in a Carriage
text: "Enjoy the room."

speaker: A Woman Who Came in a Carriage
text: Sit if you like. My waiting has nothing to do with you, or with this house. A question went out in her hand. When its answer exists, I will carry it back. Until then the fire here is a good one.

speaker: A Woman Who Came in a Carriage
text: You are carrying something with corners in your coat. Take the chair. Nobody in this house looks at what a guest sets on the table.

speaker: A Woman Who Came in a Carriage
text: She answered the card in her own hand. My mistress asked only whether the name was being sold or taken. It was being sold. The second letter went out the same evening, in her own hand again.

speaker: A Woman Who Came in a Carriage
text: "There's a lot of that trade in this city."

speaker: A Woman Who Came in a Carriage
text: A house sent me. Which house is not mine to say, and you have been in this city long enough not to ask a servant twice. I take a card out and I bring an answer back, and between those two things I keep the carriage ready and I wait.

speaker: Master Coyle
text: Your own ledger prices it. Forty gold to a 'removal man' — dated the night before your theft.

speaker: Master Coyle
text: Cups will swear to the hiring. So will Hellam — you soured his lease, and he kept the receipts.

speaker: Master Coyle
text: (Draw steel.) Then we settle it here and now.

speaker: Master Coyle
text: Another day, Coyle.

speaker: Master Coyle
text: You've a story, and no idea where it's set. Where does this 'theft' supposedly run out of, consultant? You've gone quiet. I thought as much. Come back when you've walked the ground, and we'll discuss reputations properly.

speaker: Master Coyle
text: Do you know what reputation costs in this city? More than you. Considerably more than him. Whoever sold you that story priced your discretion like an amateur and never thought to price mine at all. So. Prove it, or price your next words very carefully.

speaker: Master Coyle
text: Not for sale. The ledger goes to the Watch, the Guild, and the criers.

speaker: Master Coyle
text: Forty gold — the removal-man's rate. A retainer, and Farley's charges evaporate by morning.

speaker: Master Coyle
text: That was a better hand than I priced you for. Sit down. Please. Let us speak as adults who know what things cost. Yes — I paid for the removal; the frame was simply cheaper than the fee. Farley's sort are priced by the dozen — warehouse math, a line in anyone's book. My price would want the city's own books, all of them, and several years of them. So. Name yours. Everyone has one, and today I am buying above market.

speaker: Master Coyle
text: Enough. You've made your point in bruises — a currency I accept, though I do not respect it. Yes. I paid for the removal, and the frame was simply cheaper than the fee. There. Plainly said. Now sit down and let us discuss what your silence costs. I will pour the wine myself and open with a number you will want to hear.

speaker: Master Coyle
text: The criers will explain the rest.

speaker: Master Coyle
text: Wait. No. No, you actually mean it. You held a fortune in your hand just now and you're going to burn it — for your Mister Farley, a man in a cheap hat you've never shared a drink with. I have bought forty people in that chair. I want it noted that I offered. Get out. Take the stairs, and touch nothing on the way down.

speaker: Master Coyle
text: Stay bought, Coyle.

speaker: Master Coyle
text: Forty. Done. Worth it, too, at twice the sum. The charges were always mine to un-make; a word at the Guild, a dinner or two, and this city will have forgotten the theft by month's end. A genuine pleasure, consultant. I prefer enemies with prices. Friends run so very much dearer.

speaker: Master Coyle
text: You framed a man for your own commission.

speaker: Master Coyle
text: Your blades are groaning on a warehouse floor. Say it plainly this time.

speaker: Master Coyle
text: Just looking.

speaker: Master Coyle
text: A new face. I do like a new face — they're cheap, and occasionally they appreciate into something useful. Browsing, or selling?

speaker: Master Coyle
text: Come to inventory the wreckage? The Guild took the charter, the criers took the rest. I hope the hat-people paid you properly for it.

speaker: Master Coyle
text: Ah. My consultant. Your retainer is current and your silence is appreciated. My door — regrettably — is always open to you. Wine?

speaker: The House Factor
text: "Early. I can wait."

speaker: The House Factor
text: "Neither. I'm only warm."

speaker: The House Factor
text: Then you're early or you're late. Somebody in this room has already counted. I haven't heard which.

speaker: The House Factor
text: "Understood."

speaker: The House Factor
text: Mind it well, {addr}. Nobody in this room raises their voice and nobody in this room has ever seen a thing. Third peg by the fire's been holding the same coat since Wintersday. Nobody's asked about that either.

speaker: The House Factor
text: "Then I'll mind it until he is."

speaker: The House Factor
text: Warm is a good answer. The gentleman who left that coat was warm too. No word yet on when he'll be back for it. The coat's paid for through the season.

speaker: The House Factor
text: "Fair terms."

speaker: The House Factor
text: Busy enough. Silver rank drinks free the night they make it, once. The rest pay the board price, and we don't ask past that.

speaker: The House Factor
text: "I was told to wait on somebody."

speaker: The House Factor
text: "Busy house."

speaker: The House Factor
text: You'll want the long table, {addr}. That's the waiting table. This one's mine, and the gentleman who shares it didn't wait for anybody. Take whatever seat's open down that end.

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: "Thirty, then."

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: Thirty and it is yours, and you will get no receipt and no complaint. Take it off the cloth yourself, now, while the alley is quiet. Put it away. Deeper than that.

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: The brass is off the cloth and inside your coat before the sentence ends. He talks on to the space where you were standing.

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: Let him finish the sentence. Walk while he is enjoying it.

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: The house has had nothing behind it for forty years, and the name was doing no work, and nobody was missing it, and I would go so far as to say I did that family a kindness, all things considered.

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: The brass goes into your pack still warm from his hand. Two initials, cut deep, worth thirty gold and a fallen house's whole remaining credit.

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: "Name your price for the block."

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: [Charming Smile] Tell him what the card cost her.

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: [Stealth] Take it off the table while he is still explaining.

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: "Then it goes the other way."

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: "Sit there a while longer."

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: I cut blocks. A block is brass. What a man presses it into is between him and whoever reads the letter. That house has had nothing behind it since before I was born. The initials sat unused all that while, so I cut a block and I have rented it out since. Nobody living had a better claim, that I could find.

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: You have the block. I have a table and a story about a bad season. I would as soon we left it there.

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: "You've been renting a house's initials."

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: "Wrong table."

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: Whatever it is, I can have it on paper by this evening, and nobody will ever prove I wrote it. Eleven years at this table. The Watch has my name, and my rates for that matter, since I have never hidden the rates. Nothing to pin to any of it, though they have come and looked.

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: The block is gone off my table and the cloth is sitting there with nothing on it, which in this city means nobody so much as slows down walking past. I keep smoothing the cloth anyway. There is a cleaner square in the middle where it sat.

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: Two of my men on the paving and my table in the gutter behind them. You could have simply bought it. I would have taken almost anything.

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: He puts the brass in your hand and keeps his own hand out a moment longer, as if the table might want it back.

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: "I'll tell them it was handed over."

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: Then take the brass and take it now, before anybody thinks to ask me where it went. I have been careful for eleven years about which names I borrow and I have never once borrowed upward. Tell them the block was destroyed. Tell them a bad season did it.

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: "Far enough that somebody with an estate in this city knows your handwriting now."

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: A card. To her. Cream, was it, and one line on it? I remember the stock. I did wonder at the time how far the paper would travel. Then the next customer sat down and I had a cut to price.

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: "Call them."

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: "The brass, a while longer."

speaker: A Man with a Rented Table
text: It can. I keep two men at the mouth of this alley for exactly the conversation you are about to have, and they are paid by the week whether they work or not. Shall I call them, or would you like to look at the brass a while longer first?

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: "That's a house asset too."

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: She has not replied. She will not. That is not how any of it works and I would not have the first idea what to do with a reply if one came. What I have instead is a card in a drawer with my own name on the back of it. I have taken it out twice this morning already. I could not tell you why.

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: "I'll see you, then."

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: Three, then. Do not tell me the third one is the ring. I would have to be gracious about it and I have used all of that up this week.

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: "What is it you're holding?"

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: "He'll set it. He wanted the true thing said first, and it's said."

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: "I stood at his bench while he laid the ward. It's set properly."

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: "Your mother's stone was real. I have it back."

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: "You've been holding that card since I came in."

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: "I have the hand that did it."

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: "The card is answered."

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: "Another time."

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: I have been sitting in a paper shop for an hour. On this street it is the one room where a woman may hold something closed and nobody asks her to open it. You are the first person to stop at this table.

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: You went, then. Sit down and tell me what he said. Every word, please. People have been giving me the polite half of things for forty years.

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: It sits differently on the chain. I noticed before I looked. You were paid for the silver. Thank you for the remainder.

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: I have not put the card down since it came. The answer I keep putting off. The corner of it is going soft where my thumb sits.

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: A clerk with a good hand and a rented block. Forty years of keeping very still, and it was a man renting my mother's initials by the hour to people who wanted a door opened.

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: I answered it in my own hand. Two lines and no apology in either of them. That is the first thing I have signed in eleven years that nobody had to be told about afterwards.

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: "I'll take it."

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: "Keep it. I don't need paying for this."

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: "In a moment."

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: Then it is done, and done in the open, which I did not expect and did not know I wanted. Here. My mother had a second piece, plain, honest, worth a tenth of the first and worn twice as often. I would rather it went to somebody who earned it. It has spent long enough in the box.

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: "I'll tell him."

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: There is an enchanter with a bench in the alleys who will not touch a piece until somebody in the transaction tells him the truth about it. He is right to insist and I cannot be the one who does it. Twenty five gold when it is set. Do not be charming at him. My house is down to two assets. The name is one. The other is the habit people have of not looking past it. Tell him the truth of the stone and keep the name out of his order book.

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: "I'll start with the scribe."

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: Somebody has, and it has been out in this city doing business without me for long enough that a woman who notices everything has seen it. I will not answer that card until I can say who. Start at the counter of this very shop. There is a scribe there who rents a blank seal by the hour and who has never once asked me how I am.

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: "And did you sign something?"

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: It came to my rooms before breakfast. Cream, no crest on it, one line, in a hand I have seen twice in my life on paper I was not supposed to be holding either time. It asks me to confirm a signature.

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: "So somebody's been signing with your name."

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: I have signed nothing of consequence since the year my mother died. I am not going to say whose hand it is in a shop with a scribe in it. You already know which house I mean, because I told you where this city is run from and you did not laugh at me. She does not write to people like me. She writes about them, and only once something with her attention on it has started to move.

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: "It'll be off the table today."

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: A rented block and a good hand. I am not angry at him. There were larger people to be angry at, forty years of them, and he is very small. Take the block off whatever table it is sitting on and I will answer the card myself, in my own hand, which is a thing I have been putting off doing for a very long time.

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: "Then why have it set at all?"

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: My mother's. The stone in it is glass. I have known since I was nineteen and I have never once said so out loud, and I am not going to begin by saying it to a jeweller who will write it on an order. This city is run from a house you cannot see from any street in it, by a woman who notices everything worth noticing. A glass stone is exactly the right size to stay beneath that notice. I intend to keep it there.

speaker: A Lady with a Ring Box
text: Because she wore it to every hard thing she ever did and it never once let her down. The stone was glass for all forty of those years. It did not matter then and I will not let it start mattering now. I want the setting held properly. The stone can stay glass.

speaker: narrator
text: "Who's refusing the work?"

speaker: Wilovan
text: I'll take it.

speaker: Wilovan
text: Why bring it to me?

speaker: Wilovan
text: Not my fight.

speaker: Wilovan
text: A merchant of standing, {addr} — Master Coyle, of Coyle and Sons, though the sons are decorative. He commissioned a quiet removal of certain goods. The removal went exactly as paid for. The arrest afterward did not: our Mister Farley sits in a Watch cell for a theft he was hired to perform by the man now weeping loudest about it. We apologize in advance for imposing, {addr}. The Brothers cannot abide a frame. The hat brim dips a fraction and comes back level.

speaker: Wilovan
text: I'll tell her.

speaker: Wilovan
text: Ah. That. Settled, then, and Cups need not have worried herself over it. The chit goes somewhere inside his coat without appearing to cross the space between. Tell her the account's closed, {addr}. Tell her we said so kindly.

speaker: Wilovan
text: That phosphor pendant, then. (20 gold)

speaker: Wilovan
text: Nothing today.

speaker: Wilovan
text: For a marker-holder, {addr}, always. One piece worth mentioning came through recently — sewer work, but honest sewer work, if you follow. No questions asked on either side of the counter.

speaker: Wilovan
text: Shelf's thin, {addr}, and likely stays so. The banded chest by the wall, though — my colleague keeps it interesting for friends of the house.

speaker: Wilovan
text: Nothing new on the shelf since your pendant, {addr}. Good stock finds us slowly. Do check back.

speaker: Wilovan
text: My thanks, Wilovan.

speaker: Wilovan
text: Sold, {addr}, and quietly. Wear it in good health, and should the light draw questions, come see us before you answer them.

speaker: Wilovan
text: Come with me.

speaker: Wilovan
text: I'll go alone.

speaker: Wilovan
text: {Addr}, I'd come gladly — once we know precisely which building we're walking into. A Brother doesn't blunder in blind, whatever the invitation. Find the place first.

speaker: Wilovan
text: {Addr}. Say the word and I'll come along — an invitation this personal, a Brother answers in person. I won't dress up what happens once we're through that door: hats off, and I do mean it literally.

speaker: Wilovan
text: "I'll carry it."

speaker: Wilovan
text: "And if it goes wrong?"

speaker: Wilovan
text: "Another evening."

speaker: Wilovan
text: There is, {addr}, and I'll ask your pardon before I describe it, because describing it is most of the offence. A small parcel wants to be somewhere else by morning. The man expecting it drinks at the Adventurer's Rest. House rule there is that nobody raises a voice. We hold to it. So does everybody who owes them a table.

speaker: Wilovan
text: "Three exchanges. Nobody said a word that mattered."

speaker: Wilovan
text: "Hat on the peg, coat on the chair. Nobody looked up."

speaker: Wilovan
text: "It went loud. The hat came off. It's still done."

speaker: Wilovan
text: "Not yet."

speaker: Wilovan
text: It is, {addr}, and I had it from a man I pay to be certain. Tell me how the room took it, and I'll know what I owe you.

speaker: Wilovan
text: "Understood."

speaker: Wilovan
text: Then here are the manners of it. You don't name the thing and you don't name the man. Hat stays on, {addr}, door to door, and the room will read it. Ah — and you don't hurry. A man nearly forgot the one that matters most.

speaker: Wilovan
text: "Let's hope not."

speaker: Wilovan
text: Then the hat comes off, {addr}, plain and slow, and everybody in the room reads it correctly and steps back a pace. I'd rather it didn't come to that. My colleague holds the other opinion, which is the reason he isn't going.

speaker: Wilovan
text: Recover a name. Go on.

speaker: Wilovan
text: Remind me of the three doors.

speaker: Wilovan
text: Where do I even start with him?

speaker: Wilovan
text: Coyle's answered for it. Farley's name is clear.

speaker: Wilovan
text: Evening.

speaker: Wilovan
text: Cups asked me to see something back to you.

speaker: Wilovan
text: Anything come through lately? (Show the marker.)

speaker: Wilovan
text: "Anything wanting a quiet pair of hands?"

speaker: Wilovan
text: "The package is where it ought to be."

speaker: Wilovan
text: Begging your pardon, {addr}, a moment of your evening. We don't steal, whatever you've heard. We recover. Tonight we'd like to recover a man's good name — his, and ours with it.

speaker: Wilovan
text: Evening proper now, {addr}. The Brothers keep gentler hours after dark, present company excepted.

speaker: Wilovan
text: Evening, {addr}. The city's ears are long this week — how goes our small disagreement?

speaker: Wilovan
text: {Addr}. The parlor door is never shut to you, the alleys are safe as churches. Safer, if anything — we keep better hours. And a man remembers. All of us remember.

speaker: Wilovan
text: And this marker?

speaker: Wilovan
text: Glad Farley's out.

speaker: Wilovan
text: So we heard, {addr}. Mister Farley walked out this morning, hat restored to him at the gate. My colleague brushed the cell dust off the brim first and took his time about it.

speaker: Wilovan
text: So we heard, {addr}, the criers had it by breakfast and the Merchant's Guild by lunch. Coyle's name is worth nothing in this city now. Wilovan takes his hat off, plain and slow, and doesn't set it back on right away. He holds it to his chest, crown out, and lets the room watch him do it. Mister Farley walked at dawn — that's Farley's ceremony. This one's mine, {addr}, for a man who held a fortune in his hand and burned it for a stranger in a cheap hat. We don't often get to mean it this way.

speaker: Wilovan
text: Quietly withdrawn, {addr}, charges and all, and a man notices your purse rides heavier than it did. We admire that, on occasion, and this is one of the occasions. Wilovan takes his hat off too, the same unhurried motion, though there's something closer to approval than respect in it this time. Mind he stays bought, {addr} — gentlemen of Coyle's sort go back on a purchase the moment going back is cheap, so look in on him now and again. We will be doing the same.

speaker: Wilovan
text: A pleasure doing business, Wilovan.

speaker: Wilovan
text: A Brother's marker, {addr}. Wood and tin, and worth rather more than its materials. Shown in the alleys, trouble will beg your pardon and step around you. Shown at the parlor, a man can find you things the shops pretend not to stock — recovered things, {addr}, of impeccable provenance. Keep it dry, for the wood's sake. We don't cut replacements.

speaker: Wilovan
text: Fair enough.

speaker: Wilovan
text: {Addr}. A man can hardly accuse a fellow he hasn't found. Walk the city a while — ask around, look past the front door, and come back once you know where Master Coyle actually keeps his business. Then we'll speak of doors.

speaker: Wilovan
text: The warehouse, then. Will you come?

speaker: Wilovan
text: One more thing.

speaker: Wilovan
text: I'll pick my door.

speaker: Wilovan
text: Doors, {addr}, as a man might put it — a fellow in Coyle's position leaves several ajar. The true ledger lives at the counting-house off Wister's Alley, and paper doesn't lie; his says he paid for the theft himself. Then there's the fixer called Cups, who pours rumor by the alley gate. Coyle has soured more partners than tea has leaves, and testimony can be arranged. Politely arranged. A man meant to stop there, {addr}. There's also his warehouse crew. Should you open that particular door, a man would be honored to attend.

speaker: Wilovan
text: Fair. I'll take it.

speaker: Wilovan
text: I'll sleep on it.

speaker: Wilovan
text: Because you're not us, {addr}, and we mean that as flattery. Every hand in this brotherhood is known to the Watch by its glove size. A stranger's word will actually get listened to. Also — and a man says this with affection — things happen to you, {addr}. We have watched it happen twice since Tuesday. We'd like to point you at Master Coyle and observe.

speaker: Something in the Dark
text: [Strike first.]

speaker: Something in the Dark
text: [Back away.]

speaker: Something in the Dark
text: Silk parts overhead. Something black and silver drops the last few feet without a sound, legs unfolding to twice your height. They named it for the King it caught out hunting. Eight points settle on the stone, and it covers half the distance to you in one step.

speaker: Klbkch
text: "Resting isn't supposed to achieve anything."

speaker: Klbkch
text: "You're doing it correctly, Klbkch."

speaker: Klbkch
text: Guardsman Klbkch. Off duty for another three hours. I have been sitting for forty minutes. I am not yet certain what I have achieved.

speaker: Klbkch
text: "Then stop counting and sit."

speaker: Klbkch
text: Then I would like to know what it is supposed to do. Relc says the point is that there is no point, which is what he says about anything he has not thought about. So I have measured instead. Eleven people have laughed since I sat down. Not one has looked at the door. On a street I would report that. Here, apparently, it is normal. I am still counting.

speaker: Klbkch
text: "File it under a good night."

speaker: Klbkch
text: Thank you. I will record the evening as follows. A meal was carried to me by someone who was not required to carry it, and I was not required to ask. The bowl is warm. I will sit a while longer.

speaker: Krshia
text: There's more.

speaker: Krshia
text: I'll find it.

speaker: Krshia
text: Good. Sewer grates, south of here. Start there. Careful of teeth.

speaker: Krshia
text: That's all. My thanks, Krshia.

speaker: Krshia
text: Sold. Wear it and use it. Mending costs extra. Anything else catch your eye?

speaker: Krshia
text: My thanks, Krshia.

speaker: Krshia
text: That one, I do not ask questions about. Silverfang trade brings stranger things than that through Liscor. It came in under the wool two winters back and it has sat under that cloth since. Yours now. Wrap it before you carry it. It hums against tin, yes?

speaker: Krshia
text: That copper ring. Can't hurt. (4 gold)

speaker: Krshia
text: The handline, for the pond. (4 gold)

speaker: Krshia
text: The whetstone. (5 gold)

speaker: Krshia
text: The wax-sealed ward, then. (9 gold)

speaker: Krshia
text: The silver-capped fang. (14 gold)

speaker: Krshia
text: The stone-scale, the one under the counter. (35 gold)

speaker: Krshia
text: That piece under the far cloth. What is it? (18 gold)

speaker: Krshia
text: Back to the regular stall.

speaker: Krshia
text: That stone with the Pallass stamp on the wrapping. (18 gold)

speaker: Krshia
text: The charmed stock costs more because it does more. Wear too much of it at once and it starts to argue with itself, so choose with sense. Coin on the counter, same as the rest.

speaker: Krshia
text: That's all I'm asking.

speaker: Krshia
text: Hrr. South. Grain, salt, hide-thread, and a cart that does not stop where anyone is counting. You will not say whose hands take it, and I will not ask, yes? I will price it as wool.

speaker: Krshia
text: I'll look into it.

speaker: Krshia
text: What's the story with the inn's order?

speaker: Krshia
text: The camp south needs winter stores. Move a quiet run for them. [Charming Smile]

speaker: Krshia
text: Stand the cost of a quiet run south myself. (8 gold)

speaker: Krshia
text: The scavengers dragged it into a cellar. I've seen it myself. (Light)

speaker: Krshia
text: Your crate's accounted for.

speaker: Krshia
text: The inn's order ran short. Extend it, for Lyonette's sake. [Charming Smile]

speaker: Krshia
text: Just cover the shortfall myself. (2 gold)

speaker: Krshia
text: What's on the stall today?

speaker: Krshia
text: Just visiting.

speaker: Krshia
text: Silverfang. That's your tribe?

speaker: Krshia
text: You said the necklace was a promise.

speaker: Krshia
text: I've a few things I don't need. Buying?

speaker: Krshia
text: Hrr. My crate. Gone from the storeroom three nights past. Sewers, I think. There are scavenger tracks at the grate behind the fish stalls, and the bars are bent wide.

speaker: Krshia
text: Stall closes with the light. Come back at a decent hour, or knock loud enough I know it is not the wind.

speaker: Krshia
text: You come back. Any word on my crate?

speaker: Krshia
text: Crate is home. You, I will remember. Yes.

speaker: Krshia
text: So you went in with your fists and asked your questions after. Loud, that. But the crate is home, and nothing in it rattles loose.

speaker: Krshia
text: You found it with your own eyes and no knuckles spent. That is sharper than most bring me. Where did you learn to look first?

speaker: Krshia
text: You sent the Watch to do it for you. Sensible. It came home on a Watch cart, stamps whole. This goes in my ledger, with the debts I owe.

speaker: Krshia
text: You have the look of someone come to ask a favor. Speak plainly. I have no patience for the other kind.

speaker: Krshia
text: The inn's order, extended. For the barmaid's sake, and yours. It goes out on the morning cart, with the flour.

speaker: Krshia
text: Full hands. I'd like to see that.

speaker: Krshia
text: Back to business.

speaker: Krshia
text: Between us and the wool.

speaker: Krshia
text: So you remembered. Hrr. Then hear a little of it. Every coin this stall clears past its keep goes toward something for the tribes. Something Gnolls have been told we cannot have. We save for it anyway. There is a gathering, some years off. I mean to stand up at it with full hands. That stays between you, me, and the wool.

speaker: Krshia
text: Back to business.

speaker: Krshia
text: Not a word, Krshia.

speaker: Krshia
text: You will, if the city behaves and the thieves stay bored. And you are now a keeper of Silverfang business. For you, the front-of-stall price is the back-of-stall price. Come early on market days. The good stock does not sit past noon.

speaker: Krshia
text: What's the promise?

speaker: Krshia
text: Back to business.

speaker: Krshia
text: It suits you.

speaker: Krshia
text: My tribe, yes. Plains east and south of here — many hearths, one name. I am a Gnoll with a stall in Liscor, and the tribe is still mine. The necklace is a promise I carry.

speaker: Krshia
text: Back to business.

speaker: Krshia
text: Then I'll keep coming back.

speaker: Krshia
text: That promise, you may ask about when you have known me longer than one crate. Hrr. The wool wants restacking before the rain comes. Hand me the bolt by your elbow.

speaker: Krshia
text: My thanks, Krshia.

speaker: Krshia
text: Guild paper and a Silverfang stone, together — the city won't ask twice. Keep both on you until the Door has done its work.

speaker: Krshia
text: The old charm-cord, then. (5 gold)

speaker: Krshia
text: The hunting bow, then. Gnoll-strung, proper draw. (18 gold)

speaker: Krshia
text: That Silverfang hunting knife. Good steel. (15 gold)

speaker: Krshia
text: The wool-lined cloak. The wet gets in, out on the road. (18 gold)

speaker: Krshia
text: The boiled-leather jerkin. (24 gold)

speaker: Krshia
text: Show me the charms.

speaker: Krshia
text: Nothing today.

speaker: Krshia
text: The old charm-cord, friend's price. (4 gold)

speaker: Krshia
text: That Silverfang hunting knife, friend's price. (13 gold)

speaker: Krshia
text: The wool-lined cloak, friend's price. (16 gold)

speaker: Krshia
text: The boiled-leather jerkin, friend's price. (22 gold)

speaker: Krshia
text: Silverfang goods. Best in Liscor, and I will hear no argument on it. Cheapest at the front, the good stock where a browsing hand drifts. Coin on the counter and it is yours. No discounts, no haggling. I remember faces.

speaker: Krshia
text: Thank you, Krshia.

speaker: Krshia
text: For the barmaid, then. She is prickly, that one, but she works. I have watched her learn it. The order goes out full, and no word of the shortfall reaches Erin from my stall. You speak plainly and you speak for a friend. I respect both. It leaves with the morning cart.

speaker: Krshia
text: Thank you, Krshia.

speaker: Krshia
text: Coin instead of words. Simpler, some days. The order goes out full and Erin hears nothing of the shortfall. We are square, you and I.

speaker: Krshia
text: Glad to help.

speaker: Krshia
text: Yes. This is mine. Stamps whole, lid tight. My thanks. Take that corner — it goes behind the counter.

speaker: Krshia
text: Back to business.

speaker: Krshia
text: Understood.

speaker: Krshia
text: The inn's shortfall, yes. Smooth it here at my stall, or settle it your own way. Either gets Lyonette her full order.

speaker: Krshia
text: That's handled on my end. Go tell Lyonette, back at the inn, before Erin hears it from someone else.

speaker: narrator
text: Show me the stall again.

speaker: Krshia
text: "Closed the stall early?"

speaker: Krshia
text: "Rest easy, Krshia."

speaker: Krshia
text: A Human inn, and the food does not insult me. I walked up from the stall, and there is nobody haggling in my ear, yes?

speaker: Krshia
text: "Least I could do."

speaker: Krshia
text: Hrr. Hot through, and full to the lip. The Silverfangs remember generous hands.

speaker: Krshia
text: "Wise. Goodnight."

speaker: Krshia
text: The market was done an hour before I closed. Push past that and nothing sells. Buyers smell the desperation on a stall, yes? So this Gnoll sits and eats. Tomorrow the town can come find the stall. The shutters are down and the weights are in their box.

speaker: Ksmvr
text: Good to meet you, Ksmvr.

speaker: Ksmvr
text: I am Ksmvr. I am a member of the Horns of Hammerad. There are four of us. Four is a better number than three, because it divides. The fourth is the [Necromancer] who reads our doors, and he maintains he is hired rather than ours, on the grounds that he invoices us. Captain Ceria has ruled that he is a teammate who invoices. I have written down both positions.

speaker: Ksmvr
text: The construct was very large. I stabbed it anyway. Captain Ceria says this is called 'initiative.'

speaker: Ksmvr
text: The plates go quiet behind you, one after another, and stay quiet. Whatever they were counting, they have stopped.

speaker: Ksmvr
text: Follow exactly. Left, then straight.

speaker: Ksmvr
text: Not yet.

speaker: Ksmvr
text: I understand. I will step only where you have said. If I am wrong, I apologize in advance.

speaker: Ksmvr
text: Good.

speaker: narrator
text: I did not die. This is the preferred outcome.

speaker: Lyonette
text: Fair enough. Go on.

speaker: Lyonette
text: Maybe later.

speaker: Lyonette
text: A barmaid hears everything worth hearing in this city. But fine - go in blind if you prefer.

speaker: Lyonette
text: Anytime, Lyonette.

speaker: Lyonette
text: Done. Truly done. I keep waiting for you to name a price, and you don't. Do you know how strange that is to me? Where I'm from, a favour like this would have gone into a ledger before you'd even agreed to it. Here. It's what I could scrape together, and no, I'll not hear a word against taking it. Thank you. And not the court kind. The real one. The kitchen's still warm. Go and have the end of the bread.

speaker: Lyonette
text: Advice about the Guild? From a barmaid?

speaker: Lyonette
text: Go on.

speaker: Lyonette
text: Maybe later.

speaker: Lyonette
text: Something's got you rattled. What is it?

speaker: Lyonette
text: The supplier's scavenger trouble is dealt with - your order's on its way.

speaker: Lyonette
text: I smoothed it over with Krshia. The shortfall's covered.

speaker: Lyonette
text: I stretched the order in the kitchen. No one will know it ran short.

speaker: Lyonette
text: If you're headed to the Guild, there's something worth hearing, and it costs you nothing.

speaker: Lyonette
text: You'll do fine at the Guild - just remember what I told you.

speaker: Lyonette
text: Don't. Don't say the word 'order' too loudly. If Erin hears of it before it's fixed I will simply die on the spot. Tell me you've sorted it.

speaker: Lyonette
text: There you are. The supply matter. Handled, and quietly. I won't forget that you did that.

speaker: Lyonette
text: How bad is it, really?

speaker: Lyonette
text: I'll see it done.

speaker: Lyonette
text: I under-counted the week's supply order. I was raised to run a household larger than this inn. I cannot count a grocery list. It's short, and Erin trusts me to run this without her checking. It can still be made right before she notices. The supplier - Krshia's people - has scavengers picking at their stores in the south market. Clear that trouble by force and the delivery comes free and full. Or you smooth it over with Krshia herself, and she extends the order on a good word. Or - I should have opened with the simplest - if you can cook, stretch what we have in the kitchen so the shortfall never shows. Pick whichever suits you. Only be quick.

speaker: Lyonette
text: Sorry — one more thing.

speaker: Lyonette
text: Noted.

speaker: Lyonette
text: Selys respects competence. Keep your answers short and skip the small talk.

speaker: Lyonette
text: Selys respects competence. Stand like you've held a line before - which, evidently, you have - and skip the small talk.

speaker: Stone Golems
text: [Strike first.]

speaker: Stone Golems
text: Show the filed forge permit. Let the carving read it.

speaker: Stone Golems
text: [Back away.]

speaker: Stone Golems
text: Two grey shapes flank a stall of unclaimed crates, carved plating catching the tier's flat light. Neither has moved since you first looked. Both faces come around to you at the same moment, on the same silent hinge.

speaker: Octavia
text: Anything else?

speaker: Octavia
text: That is all.

speaker: Octavia
text: Corked and honest. Do not drink the solvent straight — one person did that once and I am still not allowed back in that inn. I mean it about the solvent.

speaker: Octavia
text: Thanks, Octavia.

speaker: Octavia
text: And it holds. Look at that. First try, no fire. Nobody crying, either. You have the knack, which is more than I can say for half of Celum. Keep at it — mix enough of these and one night you wake up with a class. Xif keeps his benches right there. Go make a mess of your own.

speaker: Octavia
text: That solvent phial. (6 gold)

speaker: Octavia
text: A twist of mineral salts. (6 gold)

speaker: Octavia
text: Show me how you make these.

speaker: Octavia
text: Just browsing.

speaker: Octavia
text: You look like someone who could use a potion. Everyone can use a potion. Mine are very reasonably priced and only occasionally on fire — once. The scorch is still on the counter. Solvent or salts, six gold either way. What do you need?

speaker: Octavia
text: Back already. Told you it gets in the blood. What are we mixing today?

speaker: Octavia
text: A paying customer, my favorite kind. Anything else, or do you want to see how these actually get made?

speaker: Octavia
text: Low flame. Steady hands.

speaker: Octavia
text: Maybe later.

speaker: Octavia
text: Okay. Real talk, because you actually bought something and that buys you the good lesson. Measure everything before it touches the flame. It will hiss at you. When it does, keep your hands level and keep pouring. Here, take the bench — cheap reagents, low flame. Watch my hands, then do exactly what I did, step by step.

speaker: Olesm
text: "Counting exits on your evening off?"

speaker: Olesm
text: "Sit closer to the fire, Olesm."

speaker: Olesm
text: Oh, good, a friendly face. I promised myself one night off and I have spent it counting how many people can reach that door before I can.

speaker: Olesm
text: "Eat something before it goes cold, then."

speaker: Olesm
text: Every room is a position, and I never asked to see them that way. Your hearth is the strong square. The stairs I haven't worked out yet — an open file, possibly, but I keep revising it. Whoever sits with their back to the door is brave or new. It happens on its own, and my stew goes cold in the meantime.

speaker: Olesm
text: "Any time, Olesm."

speaker: Olesm
text: Oh. That is properly hot. I had it in my head I would eat later. I've been saying later for three hours. Thank you. Really — thank you.

speaker: Olesm
text: I'll take him.

speaker: Olesm
text: Understood.

speaker: Olesm
text: I mapped your ledge sketches against the city plans. There's a gallery below the cisterns older than Liscor's walls, and something has been widening it. Kill it, chase it off — or map it, a map would serve. The one fixed term: it does not follow you up. Take Relc. Please.

speaker: Olesm
text: You lost, and you're pleased?

speaker: Olesm
text: Back up a moment.

speaker: Olesm
text: Another time.

speaker: Olesm
text: Both sides, yes. It's the only honest way to learn how the enemy thinks. You have to want to win as them. A human beat me across this very board once, so thoroughly I nearly thanked her. I did thank her. Best thing to happen to my game in years.

speaker: Olesm
text: Back up a moment.

speaker: Olesm
text: Another time.

speaker: Olesm
text: I learned more from that one loss than from ten wins before it. I have the ten wins; I checked. Her game is written out in my desk, second drawer, and I take it out when a Council report has me stuck. It's out on the desk now, as it happens. The granary tally has had me stuck since yesterday.

speaker: Olesm
text: I'll look into it. Where do I start?

speaker: Olesm
text: It's dealt with. I cleared the nest myself.

speaker: Olesm
text: The Watch swept it. Captain Zevara's people handled it.

speaker: Olesm
text: I didn't fight it. I mapped it: the nest, the count, the exits. [Appraise Foe]

speaker: Olesm
text: Let me know if it turns into a something.

speaker: Olesm
text: I'll keep an ear out.

speaker: Olesm
text: Worried is the professional term, yes. The market's had reports: things moving under the grates, a cistern gone foul, a fishmonger who swears something looked back at him from the dark. Probably nothing. But it is under a walled city, and I would like to be certain. Actually — you're standing here and you're armed. Would you go down and settle it?

speaker: Olesm
text: You're back. The cisterns. Any word? The grate's open now, and I still have no count for what's nesting down there.

speaker: Olesm
text: There's dust on you from somewhere below street level. The nest under the market. Is it settled? Tell me straight.

speaker: Olesm
text: Word from the gate says the Watch moved on the cisterns. Was that your doing? I want to hear how it fell out.

speaker: Olesm
text: You came back with your skin and, unless I misread you, with a picture in your head. You mapped it, didn't you. Show me.

speaker: Olesm
text: The cisterns are off my ledger and onto the Council's, thanks to you. Quiet streets. I could get used to it.

speaker: Olesm
text: Understood. I'll head down.

speaker: Olesm
text: On it.

speaker: Olesm
text: Thank you. Here's what I have. Something's nested in the old cisterns under the market — the reports say spiders, big ones, silver-backed, the kind that climb up from the Dungeon when a wall cracks. You get down there by the green sewer-grate off the south square. It's rusted, but it'll open now that someone official wants it open. As for settling it, I genuinely don't mind how. Put a blade through it, or get the Watch to sweep it. Or just bring me a proper picture of what's down there — count, size, exits. I can plan from a page like that, and it costs less in bandages than fighting does. Settle it however suits you, then come tell me it's done.

speaker: Olesm
text: Anytime, Olesm.

speaker: Olesm
text: Then it's over, and the city's quieter for it. Nobody thanks anyone for this kind of work. So let me do it here: you've the Council's gratitude, and mine, which comes with more paperwork attached. If you ever want a game, or a job that needs a clear head, you know where the board is.

speaker: Olesm
text: Glad it's useful.

speaker: Olesm
text: Oh, this is lovely work. You counted them. Exits, chokepoints, the drop where the tunnel falls away. The problem has a shape now, and it fits on one page. The Watch goes in knowing the count and the exits before a boot touches the ladder. This goes into their brief exactly as you drew it. Take the Council's thanks — and mine, doubled, because you did it the clever way.

speaker: Olesm
text: That board. You're playing yourself?

speaker: Olesm
text: Any word on the cisterns?

speaker: Olesm
text: That Watch notice — the gallery survey. I'll take it.

speaker: Olesm
text: The gallery. It's done — and it's stranger than anyone thought.

speaker: Olesm
text: There's a ward under the city that has to go on being fed. The Watch needs to pay for it.

speaker: Olesm
text: [Appraise Foe] What's the city's real weak point?

speaker: Olesm
text: You look worried about something.

speaker: Olesm
text: Zevara sent me. The tunnels under the cisterns. What do you have?

speaker: Olesm
text: It's dead. Zevara's sealing the gallery.

speaker: Olesm
text: I'll leave you to your tally.

speaker: Olesm
text: You run half this city from that desk. You know that, right?

speaker: Olesm
text: What's next for you, Olesm?

speaker: Olesm
text: Your uncle's board notice — the gallery he means?

speaker: Olesm
text: Oh — hello. One moment; I'm three columns into a supply tally and if I lose the thread I start again from the granary. Sixty-one, sixty-two. There. Olesm, council clerk. How can I help?

speaker: Olesm
text: Still counting, this late. The tally has to balance before I sleep, and it doesn't yet.

speaker: Olesm
text: Oh — hello. You have the look of someone who counts the exits on the way into a room. A [Tactician]? Truly? I so rarely get to talk shop. Sit, sit. Well. Stand. How can I help?

speaker: Olesm
text: Still up here? The gallery won't map itself, and I'd rather you were down there with a plan than up here with second thoughts. You have the map. Go.

speaker: Olesm
text: You climbed back out. I confess I ran the odds while you were down there and did not care for them. Tell me it's over. I have a column that badly wants a number in it.

speaker: Olesm
text: The gallery's sealed and the report is filed, which means my column finally has its number. I would still rather have no construct under my streets at all, but 'under control' is a phrase I can file. My thanks, again.

speaker: Olesm
text: Back to the top.

speaker: Olesm
text: I'll take a look.

speaker: Olesm
text: My uncle's notice? That's the same gallery under the cisterns — down the green sewer-grate off the south square, same as I'd send you for the nest. He wants two things confirmed in writing: the old drainage marker, still legible or not, and whether the phosphor moss has spread past the first junction. Both, mind. If one's missing, he'll send the page back and I'll hear about it at dinner.

speaker: Olesm
text: I'd read it.

speaker: Olesm
text: Back to the top.

speaker: Olesm
text: You'll find the move.

speaker: Olesm
text: Honestly? There's a class above mine. [Strategist]. Cities write to theirs. Armies wait on them. Some nights I can almost see the shape of the level, like a move you know is on the board and cannot find yet. I've started writing to other [Tacticians]. Comparing games. Doctrine, where anyone will admit to having one. Mistakes — mine, mostly, in generous detail. It may come to nothing. Or every city ends up wanting a copy of it.

speaker: Olesm
text: Back to the top.

speaker: Olesm
text: Keep the chair out.

speaker: Olesm
text: You'd be the second subscriber. The first is me, checking for errors. Thank you. People ask what I do; you asked what I'm for. I'm leaving the second chair out.

speaker: Olesm
text: Sit. Show me.

speaker: Olesm
text: Some other time, Olesm.

speaker: Olesm
text: The board's been out since Tuesday, if you want the honest count. I'm not going to pretend otherwise. Whenever you're ready. You'll have white — let me clear the tally sheets off your side of the desk.

speaker: Olesm
text: Take the coin, Olesm.

speaker: Olesm
text: I'll find it next time.

speaker: Olesm
text: Draw accepted, and the coin with it. My position was lost — I sat with it a season, I know what you had on that board. She played on from here and took me apart. I'm entering it in the book as a draw, two gold to me, and copying the final position in beneath it.

speaker: Olesm
text: Trade the rook. Knight takes, clear the corner.

speaker: Olesm
text: Queen takes the bishop. End the threat now.

speaker: Olesm
text: Ignore the bishop. Push the pawn, threaten mate in two instead.

speaker: Olesm
text: Play it safe. Offer the draw.

speaker: Olesm
text: Here. Your rook's pinned to the corner, my bishop threatens mate in three if you sit still, and I am rather pleased with myself. Two gold on it, friendly, either way. What's the move?

speaker: Olesm
text: Set it up.

speaker: Olesm
text: Actually, another time.

speaker: Olesm
text: Not a fresh game, actually. Same position, move for move: my opening, her replies, right up to the moment I stopped seeing straight. Eleven moves in, my bishop's aimed at your king and I am, in my own defense, feeling rather clever about it. Somewhere in here she found a door I didn't. Find it again and I'll believe two people can see the same board the same way.

speaker: Olesm
text: Good game, Olesm.

speaker: Olesm
text: I got lucky.

speaker: Olesm
text: Oh. Oh no. You'd let the mate stand and walk past it. That's her move. That is exactly her move. I stared at this position for a season and you found the door in one sitting. Here — two gold. I need to write this down before it stops making sense.

speaker: Olesm
text: Another time.

speaker: Olesm
text: Safe. Sound. Exactly what I played that day, and exactly why I lost: I traded fear for fear and never once asked what she wanted. Her plan. I never once looked at her plan. Try again.

speaker: Olesm
text: Another time.

speaker: Olesm
text: The obvious answer. Take the piece and the threat dies with it. I made that exact trade against her, three games earlier, and it taught me nothing. Try again.

speaker: Olesm
text: I hope the list stays theoretical.

speaker: Olesm
text: Back to the top.

speaker: Olesm
text: The cart never stood a chance.

speaker: Olesm
text: Ha. Ha. No. I run the paperwork the Council ignores, and I'm a [Tactician] whose largest engagement to date was a supply-cart dispute. Which I won. Decisively.
